chapter_title: There is no Joy that shall remain in the World till the End.
chapter_note: Nearly the entire chapter is a compact, systematic cosmological exposition: the sun and moon cannot fully rejoice during the time of Mixture because (1) they behold the Enemy ruling, and (2) they behold the Living Soul oppressed until its final cleansing and the Enemy’s binding. Only the opening dialogue attribution is later frame material; there is no NT citation and no institutional/pastoral grafting.

paragraphs.core_text: There is not [o]ne person [existing in] the world, standing firm [i]n mixture, for whom joy remains to the end.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic/dialogue frame formula: "Once again he speaks to his disciples:"
paragraphs.temporal_note: The sentence itself is a general cosmological-anthropological claim about Mixture (fits the teaching voice), but the introductory dialogue attribution is a classic Kephalaia frame marker.

paragraphs.core_text: Not only people, even the sun and the moon, the light-givers of the heavens, [ ... ] nor are they oppressed, they know not [ ... s]et firm in a summons and an [obe]dience. Nevertheless, they too, they do not rejoice completely.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic agents (sun and moon) are treated as personified powers within the system; no citation, no institutional targeting. The rhetoric remains internal to the cosmological situation of Mixture.

paragraphs.core_text: So, one: Their eyes stare at their Enemy, they [perceiv]e him and also look at his ugly shapes. They [s]ee him, that he is alive and established and is king above and below, in secret and manifest. He does every thing that he wants according to his wil[1].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered, reasoned structure (“one:”) and description of the Enemy’s modalities (secret/manifest; above/below) reads like an older explanatory teaching layer, not a later application.

paragraphs.core_text: [The s]econd: They perceive the living soul, they see [i]t and that it is ensnared and set in a great [fetter] above and below, in the tree and in the flesh, [ ... ] with every oppression. It is being pressed, drawn near to [and] sliced and eaten as it comes up and down; from above below and from below above. It [is] despoiled and moved from body to body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second item in a structured pair; depicts the Living Soul’s oppression and cycling “from body to body” as a cosmological process (cosmos→cosmos), with no turn toward church discipline or polemic.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, because of their living soul that is loved by them and honoured of them, when they see it in oppression th[ey can] not [re]joice completely.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same causal explanation internal to the cosmic drama (luminaries’ affect tied to the Living Soul’s condition), without editorial address to an audience.

paragraphs.core_text: So, one about the soul; and one about their Enemy whom they see ruling [in] what is not his own. He is proud and satisfied with a wealth that is not his own. Indeed, due to this, they do not rejoice in total; but bear up and swallow their heart until they cleanse the living soul and take it from the Enemy's hands. Then they obliterate the Death that is their Enemy and they gather it in [and fetter it in the lump] for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative restatement of the two reasons, moving to an eschatological resolution (cleansing, removal, binding). Still fully within the system: Enemy/Death are cosmic forces, not contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: When they will chain their Enemy in the bond at the [las]t, then they will rejoice and no longer grieve from this t[ime]. Also, they become the very same as they were from the [start] for ever!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic closure of a cosmological cycle (end returns to the primordial state); no hagiographic closing formula and no pastoral/exhortative pivot, suggesting direct teaching material.
